:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.8`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noYamlEmptyMapValues`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule doesn't have a fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**warning**](/reference/diagnostics#warning).
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`yml/no-empty-mapping-value`](https://ota-meshi.github.io/eslint-plugin-yml/rules/no-empty-mapping-value.html)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noYamlEmptyMapValues": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow keys without a value in YAML maps.

When a key in a map has nothing after it, YAML reads its value as `null`.
This is usually a mistake, such as a value that was forgotten or deleted by accident.

This rule also reports values that only have a tag (such as `!!str`) or an anchor (such as `&name`),
because these values are empty too.

If the value is meant to be empty, write it out, for example as `null`, so the intent is clear.

## Examples

### Invalid

```yaml
name:
```

### Valid

```yaml
name: John Doe
nickname: null
title: ""
person: { name: John Doe }
```
